clue.text: Revolutionary movement's bare strength in trouble

indicators.note: the stripped strength word sits inside the word for trouble

parts.note: to trouble someone is to vex them

indicators.note: stripped bare, the word for strength loses its outer letters

parts.note: a forte is a person's strong point

explanation.surface: A political uprising draws on raw power in a time of crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bare' strips the outer letters off the strength word, leaving ORT, and 'in' places it within the trouble word. 'Revolutionary' is about spinning, not politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool or whirlwind is a spinning, circling motion of fluid or air.

clue.text: Academic or cleric's squalid deviance

indicators.note: squalid suggests something debased and messed up, so the letters of deviance are jumbled

explanation.surface: A scandal: some university figure or churchman indulging in sordid perversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squalid' scrambles DEVIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy to a dean may serve in a university faculty or in a cathedral chapter.

clue.text: ____ upper part of house, fixing trap inside

indicators.note: the rearranged trap goes within the word for the upper part of the house

parts.note: the covering on top of a house is its roof

indicators.note: fixing suggests rearranging or setting right, so the letters of trap are reworked

explanation.surface: Fill in the blank: a roof that has had a trap fitted inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixing' rearranges the trap letters to ATPR, and 'inside' places them after the first letter of the roof word. The blank is the definition, and the completed phrase reads naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secured against rodents getting in, as a roof with a trap fitted might be.

clue.text: Sense runs out of military command

indicators.note: runs is taken out of the military order

parts.note: eyes right is the parade-ground order to turn heads to the right
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Common sense flees from the army's top brass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R (runs, in cricket scoring) from EYES RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Whence miners go back with send-off?

parts.note: the tide going back out is said to ebb
vale is Latin for farewell, a parting salute

explanation.surface: Where do miners retreat to after a farewell party?
explanation.walkthrough: EBBW VALE is a former coal-mining town in the South Wales valleys.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in the Welsh coalfield that was home to many pit workers.

clue.text: Jeer Times reporter's open presentation that's made to last

parts.note: boo is a jeer from a crowd
by means times, as in three by four

indicators.note: a reporter speaks, so the word is as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to prise a lid is to lever it open

explanation.surface: Mock the newspaper journalist who gave an unveiling ceremony that dragged on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign BY. 'reporter's' signals a sound-alike: PRISE (to open) gives PRIZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke award handed to whoever finishes in last place.

clue.text: Equipment surfers use to be visible

definitions.text: Equipment surfers use to be visible

parts.words: Equipment surfers use to be visible
parts.note: surfers here browse the internet, and a small camera lets them be seen online

explanation.surface: Beachgoers' gear, such as bright wetsuits, that keeps them in view of lifeguards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surfers' suggests the sea; these surfers are on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small camera attached to a computer lets people online see the user.

clue.text: Much parasitism's true to life

indicators.note: much of the word, not all of it, supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A great deal of parasitic behaviour is just how nature works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much' signals that most of PARASITISM'S is used, dropping its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing something exactly as it really stands, unaltered, is being faithful to reality.

clue.text: For a starter, top soldiers on plane?

indicators.note: to top is to cut off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: men is a crossword stand-by for soldiers (other ranks)
the plane is a kind of tree, common in city streets

explanation.surface: The best troops ride first on an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' removes the M of MEN. 'plane' looks like an aircraft but is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In British menus this word names the first course, or a dish before the main.

clue.text: Leas? Piece for a few swallows only

definitions.text: Piece for a few swallows only

parts.note: leas is lease with its end cut; lease means let

explanation.surface: Pastures? A morsel only a couple of birds would bother with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' suggests birds; it means gulps. The clue word is LEASE, a let, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A small slice of meat, such as a chop, eaten in a few mouthfuls.

clue.text: Head off cop winged by lean pusher

indicators.note: flanked on both sides, so the shortened word sits within the word for lean

parts.note: a ship that leans is said to list

indicators.note: the first letter is cut off the word for the policeman

parts.note: bobby is British slang for a policeman

explanation.surface: A thin drug dealer clips a policeman's head as he passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' drops the first letter of the police word, and 'winged by' sets the rest within the lean word. 'pusher' suggests drugs; here it is someone pushing a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who campaigns to influence politicians presses a cause on them.

clue.text: Environmental researcher died in war at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of war are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naturalist lost his life in a naval battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' scrambles WAR to ARW.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian naturalist studied how creatures adapt to their surroundings.

clue.text: High tide swamps lots set back leading to A1

indicators.note: the jumbled tide engulfs the reversed word
high as in drunk or intoxicated, so the letters of tide reel about
set back means the word for lots is read backwards

parts.note: lots means many

explanation.surface: A rising tide floods land plots behind a major road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' scrambles tide to DITE, 'set back' turns the lots word round to YNAM, and 'swamps' puts that inside. A1 is a British trunk road, but also means first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something sensational or terrific, just as first-class quality is.

clue.text: Clubs and bands in joint scheme to avoid duties

indicators.note: the clubs and bands letters go inside the word for the joint

parts.note: the shank is a cut of meat from the leg
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
rims are circular bands round wheels

explanation.surface: Golf clubs and music groups band together to plot a tax dodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the clubs and bands letters after the first letter of the joint word. The answer is British military slang for shirking.
explanation.definitionFit: To shirk work, especially in the forces, by dodging one's tasks.

clue.text: Cry for attention outside Vauxhall, perhaps, by a cannabis dealer, old-style

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

indicators.note: the cry is placed around the vehicle word

parts.note: hey is a shout to catch someone's notice
Vauxhall is a British car make, so a car is an example

explanation.surface: A drug dealer shouts from outside a parked car to get a customer's notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the cry round the car. Vauxhall is a British car brand. 'cannabis dealer' looks like one phrase but splits: dealer begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic name for a chemist or pharmacist, who dispensed medicines.

clue.text: It's enough to get decay repaired around 75% of courtyard

indicators.note: the rearranged decay goes around the shortened courtyard
repaired means put back together differently, so the letters of decay are reworked
three of the four letters of the courtyard word are kept

parts.note: a quad is a college courtyard

explanation.surface: Fixing the rot round most of the quadrangle will suffice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges decay to ADECY, '75% of' keeps three letters of the courtyard word, and 'around' wraps the rearranged letters round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufficiency is the quality of being as much as is needed.

clue.text: Car space by church for important meeting

parts.note: Audi is a German car make
an en is a printing space, half an em
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A parking spot next to the church, for a significant gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a typesetting space; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal interview granted by a monarch or the Pope is a grand occasion.

clue.text: Snubbed, the footy superstar not on front of mag or binding

indicators.note: snubbed as in cut short, so the last letter of the is dropped
the word on is removed from the footballer's name

parts.note: Cristiano Ronaldo is a football megastar

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of mag

explanation.surface: A football star, ignored and missing from a magazine cover, is tied down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' cuts THE to TH; 'not' removes ON from RONALDO, leaving RALDO; 'front of' takes the M of mag.
explanation.definitionFit: Servitude or bondage is the state of being bound to a master.

clue.text: Lacking a place and money, what Neapolitan needs to make a crust?

definitions.text: what Neapolitan needs to make a crust

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter a is removed

parts.note: a piazza is an Italian public square or place
dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: Homeless and broke, how can someone from Naples earn a living?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' drops an A from PIAZZA. 'make a crust' means earn a living, but here it is literal baking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pizza from Naples starts with a base of kneaded bread mixture.

clue.text: One used to cold must remove clothing here?

indicators.note: taking off the outer covering removes the first and last letters

parts.note: a native of Siberia is accustomed to freezing weather

explanation.surface: Someone hardy in the cold has to strip off in a warm place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must remove clothing' strips SIBERIAN of its outer letters. The question mark flags 'here' as a place where stripping off would suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish-Portuguese peninsula is a warm location where shedding layers makes sense.

clue.text: What's relatively lemon-like in prime samples of Sancerre

indicators.note: only the letters at prime-numbered positions (2, 3, 5, 7) of the wine name are sampled

explanation.surface: A wine tasting where the best Sancerres taste rather citrusy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime samples of' keeps the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of SANCERRE (ANER). 'lemon' means a fool, not the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is slang for a dimwit, so more foolish is the comparative sense.

clue.text: Book country inns finally after end of December

indicators.note: after places the country and final letter behind the December letter
end of means the last letter of December

parts.note: Oman is a country in Arabia

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of inns

explanation.surface: A travel guide to rural pubs, arriving at the close of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives R, 'finally' gives S, and 'after' puts OMAN plus S after R. The Book is the New Testament epistle.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's epistle is one of the books of the New Testament.

clue.text: Player's injunction against supporter

parts.note: an injunction is a ban
a joist is a beam that supports a floor

explanation.surface: A footballer gets a court order against a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' looks like a fan; it is a structural beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays a stringed instrument with a round body, common in folk music.

clue.text: Stars start to acknowledge drink from Acapulco bar note

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of acknowledge
bar means except, so the note is excluded

parts.note: tequila is the Mexican spirit, and Acapulco is in Mexico
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Celebrities nod to a Mexican drink at the bar while a song plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' gives A; 'bar' (except) removes TE from TEQUILA. 'bar' and 'note' look musical; neither is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eagle is a constellation, a pattern of celestial bodies.

clue.text: Stuck in reverse, can't set free wheels temporarily

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the word for reverse

parts.note: the reverse side of something is its rear

indicators.note: freed from their order, the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the contraction, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Jammed in reverse gear, a driver can't escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set free' rearranges the letters of can't to NTAC, and 'Stuck in' places them within the reverse word after its first two letters. 'reverse' is a noun meaning back, not a gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hired transport is a vehicle borrowed for a short period.

clue.text: Drab person overseeing chapel was flattering

parts.note: drab and fawn are both dull light-brown shades
in newspaper trade-union jargon the workplace branch is a chapel, and the editor is the person in charge of that paper

explanation.surface: A dull clergyman running a chapel was full of compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: In British printing, a union branch is called a chapel; ED (editor) is the one in charge at the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To grovel or curry favour is to behave sycophantically toward someone.

clue.text: Fun had after descending 'suited and booted'

definitions.text: Fun had after descending 'suited and booted'

parts.words: Fun had after descending 'suited and booted'
parts.note: the descent is down a ski slope in full gear, and the fun follows at the bar

explanation.surface: Partying in formal wear after coming downstairs dressed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suited and booted' suggests smart dress; it is ski suits and ski boots.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names the socialising at resorts once the day's skiing is done.

clue.text: School of thought revealing my clue as rubbish!

indicators.note: treating the words as rubbish means scrambling the letters of my clue

explanation.surface: The setter mocks a philosophical school for deeming the clue garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as rubbish' scrambles MY CLUE. Aristotle taught in the original, near Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle's academy gave its name to institutions of learning and lecture halls.
